mmfold:
Use case: style-transfer. Create one beautiful editorial molecular watercolor/gouache illustration for a premium scientific website. David Goodsell-inspired molecular illustration language, without copying any particular artwork: softly irregular fine warm-black ink contours, organically scalloped space-filling protein silhouettes, hand-painted flat pastel patches, ONE restrained cel shadow, visible delicate watercolor paper grain INSIDE painted shapes, warm low-saturation colors. Prioritize graceful composition and painterly beauty, not literal per-atom fidelity; consolidate tiny atom details into larger readable organic lobes, varied scale and pleasing rhythm. No 3D render, no shiny balls, no glow, no halo, no neon, no glass, no gradients around objects, no particle effects, no lettering, no labels, no logo, no arrows, no connecting lines. Output ONE landscape 1200x750 RGBA image with genuine alpha=0 transparent background. Clean cutout edges. Put all artwork within x=100..1100,y=145..605, leaving generous TRANSPARENT margins. Designed to look clear and elegant on a #0F0E17 dark card; do not paint the card or a paper background.
Input image 1 is a real-coordinate structural reference ONLY, not a style reference. Reimagine this PD-L1/KN035 docked two-protein complex as a charming hand-painted molecular close-up. Preserve the broad complementary two-body silhouette and touching interface, but simplify and art-direct freely. PD-L1 left in sky blue #93C9EC, nanobody right in warm pale cream. An asymmetrical balanced central composition, the blue body slightly taller, cream body snugly meeting it. A few softly brighter painted patches at the interface, never luminous. Very few small outlined solvent dots. Organic and calm, like a considered scientific watercolor plate, with ample breathing room. Keep fine dark ink consistently readable rather than dense black stippling.

Input image 1 (mmfold.webp) and Input image 2 (moleculeos.webp) are the TWO STYLE MASTERS from this exact illustration series. Match both precisely: same fine softly irregular warm-black #0A0910 ink, same watercolor grain strength, same organic scalloped larger lobes, same one restrained shadow band, same pastel saturation. Do not copy their molecular subjects, colors, membrane or composition. Input image 3 is a REAL-COORDINATE SHAPE REFERENCE of PETase PDB 5XH3, protein chain A, with bound HEMT ligand in cream. This image defines enzyme shape and active-site location ONLY; replace its smooth computational atom balls with the painted organic lobes of images 1 and 2.
Scene: QuantaMind molecular reaction simulation. Three small vignettes of the SAME PETase enzyme active site arranged left-to-right along a gentle shallow arc, center vignette a little higher. No vignette frames, no circular panels, no separators. All three keep the SAME compact asymmetric triangular/wedge enzyme outline, low broad left flank and taller rounded right shoulder seen in image 3. The active-site cleft is a narrow, slanted recessed groove in the near-center front face, slightly right of center, running lower-left to upper-right as shown by the cream ligand in image 3. Enlarge that cleft slightly for visual readability without turning the enzyme into a torus or a hollow ring.
Each enzyme is soft lavender #B9AEF0, with the same dark warm ink and paper pigment as the series. Inside the cleft is a short warm creamy pale-gold polymer substrate, drawn as a tiny cluster-chain of smaller irregular atom lobes, distinctly smaller than the enzyme's surface lobes. In the LEFT vignette the substrate is an intact gently bent short chain entering the groove; in the CENTER it nestles slightly deeper, a subtly bent/compressed reactive center with one tiny cream water/proton-like bead close to it; in the RIGHT it is two small shortened product clusters gently separated at the groove mouth. Keep the enzyme body, camera angle, scale, coloring and active-site placement consistent across all three. Changes should be subtle, beautiful and legible: suggest before/transition/after reaction through substrate shapes and positions only, never through arrows, lines, glow or effects. This is a painterly conceptual reaction path, not a literal computed molecular trajectory.
Composition: equal-sized enzyme vignettes about 265px wide at centers near (290,410), (600,350), (910,410) on a 1200x750 canvas; all important paint in central x=100..1100,y=145..605. A handful of restrained outlined warm-gray water/ion dots around the triplet, no particle field. Calming graceful molecular landscape, lavender is the clear dominant hue, cream substrate is lighter. Transparent negative space between separate vignettes. NO text of any kind, no letters, no labels, no numbers, no arrows, no lines, no light trails, no halos, no neon, no DNA decoration. Use the two style masters to make this unquestionably the FOURTH member of the same watercolor set, not a new art direction.
